summary: Arithmetic CHOP for pre/post operations, combining channels or input CHOPs, gain/offset, range mapping, and integer conversion. It is the standard planner step for scaling, clamping, and shaping CHOP control signals.

key_params.name: preop
key_params.note: Unary operation on each channel before combine stages.

key_params.name: chanop
key_params.note: Combine channels within each input CHOP.

key_params.name: match
key_params.note: Match channels between inputs by channel number or channel name.

key_params.name: interppars
key_params.note: Interpolate parameters per sample for high-frequency input such as audio.

key_params.name: integer
key_params.note: Ceiling, floor, or round resulting values.

key_params.name: fromrange
key_params.note: Input low/high range for linear scaling.

key_params.name: fromrange1
key_params.note: Input low value for range mapping.

key_params.name: fromrange2
key_params.note: Input high value for range mapping.

key_params.name: torange
key_params.note: Output low/high range for linear scaling.

key_params.name: torange1
key_params.note: Output low value for range mapping.

key_params.name: torange2
key_params.note: Output high value for range mapping.

key_params.name: autoexportroot
key_params.note: Export root for path-style channel names.

common_gotchas: Math CHOP is arithmetic, not boolean logic; use Logic CHOP for logic operations such as and/or comparisons between channels.
Interp Pars per Sample helps avoid audio-rate pops when changing multiply, add, or range parameters on high-frequency input.
Match by and Align matter with multiple inputs; choose channel name/index matching and interval handling deliberately before combining CHOPs.
Operation order is pre-op, combine channels/CHOPs, post-op, mult/add, range, then integer conversion.
Use Scope to restrict which channels are affected instead of assuming every incoming channel should be scaled.
